records.prompt: Let \(R\) be the first-quadrant region enclosed by \(y=2x\) and \(y=x^2\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
The curves intersect at \(x=0\) and \(x=2\), so
\[
\boxed{A=\int_0^2(2x-x^2)\,dx=\frac43}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For a solid with base \(R\), the cross-sectional area perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis is \(A(x)=\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\). Find its volume.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For another solid with base \(R\), cross sections perpendicular to the \(y\)-axis are squares. Write, but do not evaluate, an integral for the volume.
parts.answer:
At height \(y\), the horizontal base length is \(\sqrt{y}-y/2\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{V=\int_0^4\left(\sqrt{y}-\frac y2\right)^2dy}.
\]

classification.primaryTopic: Area and Volumes with Known Cross Sections

records.prompt:
A twice-differentiable function \(f\) has the tabulated values
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
x&2&3&5&8&13\\\hline
f(x)&1&4&-2&3&6
\end{array}
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus,
\[
\int_2^{13}(3-5f'(x))dx=3(11)-5(f(13)-f(2))=33-25=\boxed{8}.
\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use a left Riemann sum with the tabulated subintervals to approximate \(\int_2^{13}f(x)\,dx\).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Suppose \(f'(5)=3\) and \(f''(x)<0\) on \([5,8]\). Use tangent and secant lines to show \(\frac43\le f(7)\le4\).
parts.answer:
The tangent line at \(x=5\) is
\[
y=-2+3(x-5).
\]
Because \(f\) is concave down, the graph lies below its tangent, so \(f(7)\le4\). The secant line through \((5,-2)\) and \((8,3)\) is
\[
y=-2+\frac53(x-5).
\]
A concave-down graph lies above its secant, so \(f(7)\ge-2+10/3=4/3\).

classification.primaryUnitLabel: Unit 6: Integration and Accumulation of Change

records.prompt:
The derivative of \(f\) is
\[
f'(x)=\begin{cases}
g(x),&-4\le x\le0,\\
5e^{-x/3}-3,&0<x\le4,
\end{cases}
\]
where the supplied graph of \(g\) on \([-4,0]\) is the lower semicircle of radius \(2\) centred at \((-2,2)\), and \(f(0)=5\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Inflection points occur where \(f'\) changes monotonicity. The semicircle changes from decreasing to increasing at \(x=-2\), and at \(x=0\) the derivative changes from increasing to decreasing. Thus
\[
\boxed{x=-2\text{ and }x=0}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
The area under \(g\) from \(-4\) to \(0\) is rectangle area \(8\) minus semicircle area \(2\pi\). Therefore
\[
f(-4)=5-(8-2\pi)=\boxed{2\pi-3}.
\]
Also
\[
f(4)=5+\int_0^4(5e^{-x/3}-3)dx=\boxed{8-15e^{-4/3}}.
\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For \(-4<x<4\), find the \(x\)-coordinate where \(f\) has an absolute maximum. Justify.
parts.answer:
On \([-4,0]\), \(f'\ge0\). On \((0,4]\), solve \(5e^{-x/3}-3=0\) to obtain \(x=3\ln(5/3)\). The derivative changes from positive to negative there, so
\[
\boxed{x=3\ln\left(\frac53\right)}.
\]
